note: GK bank fact (subtopic unesco_sites): inscription years — Agra Fort, Ajanta, Ellora, Taj Mahal 1983; Sun Temple Konarak 1984; Hampi and Khajuraho 1986; Humayun's Tomb and Qutb Minar 1993. All years are taught in section s2 from the PIB Annexure-I list (claims c09, c10, c15, c16, c22, c23) and practised in q08-q13.

GK bank fact (subtopic unesco_sites): Mountain Railways of India inscribed in stages — Darjeeling (West Bengal) 1999, Nilgiri (Tamil Nadu) 2005, Kalka-Shimla (Himachal Pradesh) 2008. Taught in sections s5 and s6 from the PIB Annexure-I row (claim c35) and practised in q30; the bank's own STATEMENT item (claiming Kalka-Shimla 2005) is a distractor pattern — the chapter teaches the correct pairing.

WBCS 2019 Q35: Sundarbans inscribed as World Heritage Site for its mangrove forests (correct option C). Taught in s6 from the WII Sundarban page (claims c49, c51: largest delta, 10,200 km2 of mangrove forest; Sundarban National Park core is a UNESCO World Heritage site) plus PIB list row (c48, 1987, Natural); practised in q37.

WBCS 2024 Q148: which is NOT a UNESCO World Heritage Site — Gateway of India (correct option D); Ellora Caves, Kaziranga National Park and Churches and Convents of Goa are all inscribed. Taught in s2 (claims c09, c12, c17 for the three real sites; c61 records that the Gateway of India does not appear in the official PIB list of 45) with an exam_note box; practised in q44.

WBCS 2016 Q39 asks which two Indian cities were first nominated to UNESCO's Creative Cities Network (UCCN) — Varanasi and Jaipur. UCCN is a different UNESCO programme from the World Heritage List; this chapter covers only the World Heritage List (subtopic unesco_sites), and no fetched source for this chapter covers UCCN membership. Not taught here; flagged so the Creative Cities topic can be covered where it belongs.

WBCS 2021 Q63: Khajuraho, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, was first mentioned in the 11th century by Abu Rihan Al-Biruni. The chapter teaches Khajuraho's inscription (1986, claim c15, practised in q13), but the Al-Biruni mention is a medieval-history fact that appears in none of this chapter's fetched GOVT sources, so the specific answer the PYQ demands is not taught here; it belongs to the history book's coverage of Al-Biruni.
